question: This creature's favorite food is said to be cucumbers, which practitioners of folk magic offer to appease it or ward off its attacks. It is said to enjoy challenging humans and animals to sumo wrestling matches, sometimes losing on purpose to spare a respectful opponent. According to legend, friendly members of this species taught humans the arts of medicine and bone-setting. A shallow, water-filled dish set into the top of its head is the source of its strength, which drains away if the liquid spills. A cucumber-filled sushi roll takes its Japanese name from this creature. For 10 points, name this child-sized, turtle-shelled water yokai of Japanese folklore.

This deity was born from the left eye of the god Izanagi as he purified himself after fleeing the underworld. Enraged by her brother Susanoo's destructive rampage through her rice fields and weaving hall, she withdrew into a cave, plunging the world into darkness. The other gods lured her back out with raucous laughter and a ritual dance performed by the goddess Ame-no-Uzume, tricking her into peeking out at her own reflection in a mirror. Japan's imperial family has traditionally claimed descent from her, and one of the three imperial regalia, a sacred mirror, is closely associated with her myth. For 10 points, name this Shinto sun goddess, chief deity of Japan's imperial cult and ruler of the High Celestial Plain.

Dating back to at least the Kamakura period, folklore describes this shapeshifting creature, known collectively as bake-danuki, transforming itself and its surroundings to fool unsuspecting humans, sometimes even becoming a household teakettle. Unlike the more dangerous fox spirits it's often grouped with, it's characterized as good-natured, sociable and hopelessly fond of treats and pranks rather than real menace. Statues of this animal frequently stand outside Japanese businesses, styled after the protective deity Jizo, to bring good fortune. A 1994 Studio Ghibli film follows a community of them using their shapeshifting powers to try to stop a suburban housing development from destroying their forest home. For 10 points, name this raccoon dog of Japanese folklore, the basis of the Tanooki suit power-up in the Mario franchise.
